question: The Kharchi festival is primarily associated with:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Veneration of indigenous tribal deities**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Kharchi festival is a significant cultural and religious festival in Tripura, primarily dedicated to the **veneration of 14 indigenous tribal deities**, collectively referred to as the "Chaturdasha Devata."
 
• It is observed annually at the Chaturdasha Devata Temple, located in **Old Agartala**, Tripura.
 
• The festival involves elaborate rituals, including the ceremonial bathing of the deities in the sacred river followed by their worship with traditional offerings like flowers, fruits, and animal sacrifices.
 
• The Kharchi Puja is deeply rooted in tribal traditions and signifies the cleansing of sins and the offering of gratitude to the deities for protecting the community and ensuring prosperity.
 
• The festival is celebrated over a period of **seven days** and attracts a large number of devotees, both tribal and non-tribal, symbolizing communal harmony and cultural integration in the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Worship of Lord Jagannath:**

 
 
• The worship of Lord Jagannath is associated with the famous **Rath Yatra festival**, primarily celebrated in Puri, Odisha.
 
• Rath Yatra involves the grand chariot procession of Lord Jagannath, his brother Balabhadra, and sister Subhadra, attracting millions of devotees.
 
• Lord Jagannath is a revered deity in Hinduism and is considered an incarnation of Lord Vishnu.
 
 
 
• **Commemoration of Tripura's Statehood Day:**
 
 
• Tripura's statehood day is celebrated on **21st January** every year, marking the day Tripura became a full-fledged state in 1972 under the North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971.
 
• It is an occasion of pride for the people of Tripura, highlighting the state's rich cultural heritage and socio-economic progress.
 
 
 
• **Worship of River Goddess Yamuna:**
 
 
• The worship of Goddess Yamuna is commonly associated with the festival of **Yamuna Jayanti** or Yam Dwitiya, celebrated in certain parts of India.
 
• Yamuna is considered a sacred river goddess and the sister of Yama, the god of death, according to Hindu mythology.
 
• On this occasion, devotees perform rituals and offer prayers along the banks of the Yamuna River, seeking blessings for prosperity and purification of sins.
